run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T06:49:10Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy tracks a real burst of request errors rather than a standing condition. frontend-proxy's own ERROR-status span rate (10m rate, spans/s) sat at 0.0043–0.0088 through 06:30–06:50, rose to 0.156 at 06:51 and ~0.29 across 06:52–06:59, then fell back to ~0.0072 by 07:03. The error spans are named concretely: frontend-proxy 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'; frontend 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 'POST' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder'; checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' and 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge'. The deepest failing span the evidence shows is checkout's client call to payment. frontend-proxy's access log shows the responses: no 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500' between 06:44:00 and 06:49:28, then a continuous run of '500 - via_upstream' from 06:49:28.787Z to 06:51:30.401Z, and a 200 for the same route again at 06:52:11.617Z, plus two '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on GET /api/data at 06:52:14Z. The first 500 falls in the same second as the payment Deployment rollout events: new ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f scaled 0 to 1 at 06:49:23, pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t scheduled/pulled/created/started 06:49:23–06:49:27, old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 scaled 1 to 0 and pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 killed ("Stopping container payment") at 06:49:28. Payment itself recorded 0 ERROR spans while checkout recorded 42.2 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' client-span errors in the same ten minutes, and payment logged normal 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs from 06:51:34.991Z onward, so the failing Charge calls did not produce payment-side failures. A fault-injection explanation (flagd-config currently declares paymentFailure "100%" and paymentUnreachable "on") is rejected for this burst because payment kept completing charges and recorded no error spans. What remains unverified is why the payment pod template changed at 06:49:23 and why the replacement pod only began handling charges around 06:51:3x; change history is not an available integration, the old pod's logs are gone, and the alerting rule itself is not loaded in this Prometheus. Conclusion is partial: the alert's origin is narrowed to the payment Deployment's rollout, but the trigger and the final step to the error burst rest on timing rather than direct observation.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's ERROR-status span rate (spans/s, 10m rate) was 0 at 06:29, 0.0043–0.0088 through 06:30–06:50, rose to 0.156 at 06:51 and ~0.29 across 06:52–06:59, then 0.139 at 07:00, 0.0141 at 07:02 and ~0.0055–0.0072 from 07:03 to 07:10; UNSET-status spans stayed ~21–24/s except a dip to ~6.8/s at 07:10.

In the ten minutes to 07:00 the ERROR-status spans are exactly attributable to: frontend-proxy 'ingress' 43.30 and 'router frontend egress' 40.14; frontend 'POST /api/checkout' 42.25, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 42.25, 'POST' 42.25, 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 42.25; checkout 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' 42.17 and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' 42.17.

Service-level ERROR-span increases for 06:50–07:00 were frontend 169.0, checkout 84.3, frontend-proxy 83.4, with ad 1.06, recommendation 1.05 and fraud-detection 1.05, and accounting, cart and payment at 0; in the ten minutes to 06:40 the same query gave frontend 0, frontend-proxy 2.11, recommendation 1.05, ad 0, fraud-detection 0, payment 0, accounting 0 and cart 0.

For 06:50–07:00, checkout's 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' client spans were 328.9 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET plus 42.2 with STATUS_CODE_ERROR, while payment's 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' server spans were 300.1 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET and 0 with STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

frontend-proxy's access log contains no 'POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500' line between 06:44:00 and 06:49:28 (the filtered query returned 64 lines and the earliest is 06:49:28.787536Z); from 06:49:28.787Z to 06:51:30.401Z it logs a continuous run of '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream' responses forwarded to upstream frontend 100.96.2.36:8080, and a 200 for the same route reappears at 06:52:11.617Z.

At 06:52:14.297Z and 06:52:14.421Z frontend-proxy logged '"GET /api/data/... HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for upstream frontend 100.96.2.36:8080, with normal 200 responses to other frontend routes interleaved from 06:51:57Z onward.

otel-demo events show the payment Deployment rollout: Deployment payment 'ScalingReplicaSet' scaling payment-79d86bf97f 0 to 1 at 06:49:23, pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t Scheduled 06:49:23 / Pulled 06:49:26 / Created 06:49:26 / Started 06:49:27, ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 'SuccessfulDelete' deleting pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 and Deployment payment scaling that ReplicaSet 1 to 0 at 06:49:28, and Pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 'Killing' ("Stopping container payment") at 06:49:28.

All other otel-demo pods predate the incident with 0 restarts (frontend-675fd7b5c5-f44st 06:17:29, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-b9w85 06:17:27, checkout-5dccddf8bb-k45hc 06:17:27, load-generator-57ffcd644-ss82p 06:17:28, flagd-67cdb699c-c2gw8 06:19:13); payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t started 06:49:23 with 0 restarts and is owned by ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f.

The replacement payment pod's retained log shows normal charge handling from 06:51:34.991Z onward — 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs at 06:51:34–06:52:17 and again 06:57:14–07:00:19 — and checkout's log for 06:50:30–06:52:30 shows '[PlaceOrder]', 'payment went through', 'order placed' and 'order confirmation email sent' for individual orders.

Across payment's retained log for 06:45:00–07:05:00 the only line matching error, failure, unavailable or connection terms is the exact text '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' at 2026-11-17T06:51:40.851Z (704 of 705 lines removed by the filter).

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config declares payment fault-injection settings: flag paymentFailure with defaultVariant "100%" (variants 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%, 100%, off) and flag paymentUnreachable with defaultVariant "on" (variants off, on), alongside adFailure, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure.

The payment Deployment currently reports availableReplicas 1, readyReplicas 1, updatedReplicas 1 with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment, RollingUpdate strategy maxUnavailable 25%, and env FLAGD_HOST=flagd / FLAGD_PORT=8013 / PAYMENT_PORT=8080.

The 503 signature seen in the alerting service is also pre-existing at low rate: the sampled frontend-proxy error traces returned at 06:28:33–06:36:57 show 'ingress' spans with http.status_code 503 / otel.status_code ERROR plus a 'router frontend egress' span with error="true" and http.status_code 0, with load-generator 'GET' spans also 503 and no frontend span present in those traces.

Against a payment application-failure explanation for the alert: payment recorded 0 ERROR spans in 06:50–07:00 while checkout recorded 42.2 on 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge', and payment logged completed transactions ('Transaction complete.') during the same minutes, so payment was not returning failing responses for the calls that errored at checkout.

Rejected for this burst: that the flagd fault-injection values paymentFailure="100%" and paymentUnreachable="on" were continuously in effect and caused the charge failures. A 100%/unreachable setting does not match the observed behaviour — payment had 300 charge server spans with 0 errors in the same ten minutes and logged successful charge handling, and only 42 of roughly 371 checkout charge calls errored; the ConfigMap was also read after the window, so its values cannot be dated to 06:49–06:52.

Leading hypothesis: the payment Deployment's rollout removed the only serving payment pod at 06:49:28 (old pod killed; replacement pod created 06:49:23–06:49:27) and the replacement did not handle charges until about 06:51:3x, so checkout's 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' calls in that interval failed at the connection level, producing checkout PlaceOrder errors, frontend /api/checkout 500s and the frontend-proxy request-error burst the alert reports. Support is timing-based (first 500 at 06:49:28.787Z in the same second as the kill event, last 500 at 06:51:30.401Z, charge handling logged from 06:51:34.991Z, and 0 payment-side errors), not a directly observed connection error on the checkout side.

The single payment-pod error '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' at 06:51:40.851Z is consistent with the replacement pod's own in-cluster gRPC client (its flagd provider) still re-establishing a connection during startup, since payment's 'grpc.flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' span series first appears only at 06:53:30 in the 15s-step view; whether any charge failed because of flagd is not verified.

Retrieve the payment Deployment's pod-template diff for the 06:49:23 rollout through a change-history source (not integrated here) and review payment's readinessProbe/startupProbe: with replicas=1 the old pod was terminated one second after the replacement started (Started 06:49:27, old pod Killing 06:49:28) while the replacement began serving charges only about two minutes later, so readiness may pass before the process can serve.

Confirm with the owners of the otel-demo demo whether flagd-config's paymentFailure="100%" and paymentUnreachable="on" variants are intentional; they are fault-injection settings for payment and, if anyone enables them at runtime, they would produce the same checkout Charge failure path seen here.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name="RequestErrorRate" and with type=alert each returned no rows (no_data), so the rule expression, threshold and 'for' duration, and why the alert began firing at 06:49:10Z while frontend-proxy already carried background ERROR spans (10m rate 0.004–0.009/s from 06:29), could not be verified.

The change-history integration is not available, so what changed in the payment Deployment pod template at 06:49:23 (triggering the new ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f) and when the flagd-config values paymentFailure="100%"/paymentUnreachable="on" were written are unknown; all Kubernetes object state read here is post-window.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus (get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} and kube_pod_container_info{namespace="otel-demo"} both returned no series), so image digests could not be compared to confirm a configuration-only template change; rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count likewise returned no series, so the failing gRPC status codes were not readable directly.
app_payment_transactions_total has no series in the window (get_all_labels returned nothing), so payment-side transaction outcomes are unknown beyond its logs.

The terminated pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4 no longer exists and its logs are unavailable; the replacement payment pod has no previous container instance (HTTP 400 'previous terminated container ... not found'). A log query for payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t over 06:49:20–06:50:20 returned no lines (no_data), which is a matched-nothing result and not proof the process logged nothing.

The frontend container returned no log lines in 06:47–06:57 (0 bytes read, status no_data) and the flagd containers returned no log lines in 06:40–07:05 (status no_data), so neither the frontend's error text for the /api/checkout 500s nor the flagd side of the '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' event could be examined.

Jaeger holds no spans from the 06:49–06:55 burst: the newest frontend-proxy error traces returned are from 06:28:33–06:36:57, and traces_search_by_tags for checkout error spans (error=true on 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge', and otel.status_code=ERROR) returned no traces (no_data), so the error message or detail of the failing Charge spans is unknown.

The payment Deployment's readiness and startup probe specification was not retrieved, so the reason the replacement pod could be considered ready at 06:49:28 while charging only from about 06:51:34 is an inference from log and access-log timing.

Whether the two 503 UC (upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}) responses on GET /api/data at 06:52:14Z share the payment-related cause is unknown; they are a different failure mode from the /api/checkout 500s.

frontend-proxy's Envoy access-log prefix clock is inconsistent with the collected log timestamps (prefixes read 2025-12-15T17:4x while the records are 2026-11-17T06:5x), so the row timestamps from the log API were used; the prefix timestamps are unreliable for ordering.
next_steps: Pull the payment Deployment's pod-template diff for the 06:49:23 rollout from a change-history source outside this Run to establish what actually changed and who applied it.

Review the payment Deployment's readinessProbe and startupProbe configuration against the observed one-to-two minute gap between container start (06:49:27) and first successful charge handling (06:51:34).
Ask the otel-demo demo owners to confirm whether the flagd-config paymentFailure="100%" and paymentUnreachable="on" variants are intentional, and record when that ConfigMap was last written.
Load or locate the RequestErrorRate recording/alerting rule in the Prometheus that evaluates it so its exact expression and threshold can be checked against the 0.0111 error-rate value in the alert.

If the payment pod template turns out to be unchanged, re-examine whether the rollout was a reschedule on node i-08d3ba92d08837746 and whether the old pod's termination left a connection-drain window visible in Envoy or checkout connection metrics.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
